method: Source-text reading with prior draft exposure; evidence pointers checked against the recorded source hashes. These judgments are separate from formal annotation and do not assert human review completion.
source_scope: AnnoCTR extracted text including narrative, captions and tables; linked images, external articles and underlying incident telemetry were not independently examined.
protocol: CTI_Event_Instance_Annotation_Protocol_v0.5-draft; incident-linked attack-action stratum; nearest shared resolved incident; A_120 parent mappings

reports.genre: Actor ecosystem and multi-victim activity profile
reports.assessment: Retain the report. Dated forum and publication activity is distinguishable, but it belongs to communications or infrastructure context. The exploitation, lateral movement and exfiltration sections describe an actor-level pattern across cases. The Thai and German victim references do not establish a shared incident or an ordered pair of atomic attack actions.
reports.strongest_counterargument: The narrative contains explicit sequencing and named victims. This can support a generic procedure graph, but the text does not bind that whole procedure to two identified executions in one incident.
reports.required_resolution: Keep communications and victim contexts separate. Do not use the September publication dates as attack-action times or the report-wide TTP list as event-level mappings.

reports.assessment: Retain the report. The mutex check, packet construction, file transfer and shell commands describe program behavior. Command order in a switch statement does not establish an execution order in an intrusion. The unavailable C2 further limits what the analysis observed.
reports.strongest_counterargument: The article repeatedly describes what happens first and then. Those cues support control-flow or capability relations, not by themselves distinct victim-side occurrences. Lack of C2 access alone does not prove that the malware never executed.
reports.required_resolution: Preserve capability sequences in an auxiliary description. Do not infer that all listed commands were invoked or pull unreviewed evidence from Part 1 into this fixed report.

reports.assessment: Retain the explicitly observed ordered delivery-chain candidate and the asserted website-creation action. The source reports initial Smoke Loader delivery and subsequent follow-on downloads. It does not clearly individuate one particular chain execution or bind it to an incident. Both endpoint mappings are not accepted, so the stronger shared-technique claim remains unresolved separately from the temporal evidence. RedLine and Raccoon are payload families, not proof of two executions on one host.
reports.strongest_counterargument: The source explicitly attributes follow-on download observations to its researchers. This is stronger than merely listing capabilities. The unresolved issue is occurrence and incident identity under the strict primary protocol, not an absence of any observed malicious behavior.
reports.required_resolution: Keep the ordering as a campaign-level candidate. Reconsider atomicity only with evidence identifying the occurrences; do not require a named victim as an extra rule, and do not turn a missing initial mapping into a fully omitted edge.

reports.assessment: Retain the report and separate German and South Korean contexts. Detection, submission, compilation and victim awareness are distinct from attack occurrence times. The source explicitly limits knowledge of compromise duration and reports that the South Korean payload was not found. DNS protocol steps and the appendix technique table do not resolve a primary occurrence pair.
reports.strongest_counterargument: The German compromise assessment is substantive evidence, and the report gives detailed DNS tunneling behavior. It still does not identify two particular attack executions and a relation between them; target attribution is not the same as event resolution.
reports.required_resolution: Preserve uncertain dates and target assessments. Consider code signing as a potential preparatory action, but do not infer that other related signed drivers belong to the same incident. Do not join target contexts, turn compilation dates into execution times, or propagate the report-level ATT&CK table onto every activity.

reports.assessment: Retain one identifiable email-send candidate with a source-reported date and timezone. Three document hashes describe sample variants, not three timestamped deliveries. The subsequent macro, payload and exfiltration discussion mixes conditional behavior with analysis observations and does not establish a second incident-linked occurrence paired with that send.
reports.strongest_counterargument: The source says its team observed multiple deliveries and information transfer. Those statements should not be discarded as wholly hypothetical. They remain unresolved at the individual occurrence level and cannot be connected to the named email solely by their position in the article.
reports.required_resolution: Keep the message-send candidate, campaign repetition and sample observations separate. One email exemplar does not establish a recipient-level transmission count. Preserve the June email versus July campaign-start tension. Report-level technique mappings do not establish event-level mappings.

count_interpretation: candidate_attack_occurrences counts retained identifiable candidates in this pass, not all asserted actions or a validated census; zero is not evidence of absence.
